projects.title: ShopWave — Campus Marketplace
projects.summary: A peer-to-peer e-commerce marketplace for PMU students to buy and sell textbooks, electronics, and dorm essentials.
projects.description: ShopWave is a full-stack e-commerce platform built for the Building E-Commerce course. It features product listings with image galleries, category browsing, a shopping cart, order checkout flow, seller dashboards, and an admin panel for moderating listings. The team implemented JWT-based authentication, Stripe test-mode payments, and a responsive UI built with React and Tailwind CSS, backed by a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL database.
projects.team_members: Lama Al-Otaibi, Yousef Al-Harbi, Sara Al-Qahtani

projects.title: ClinicFlow — Appointment & Records System
projects.summary: A clinic management system for scheduling appointments, managing patient records, and generating billing reports.
projects.description: ClinicFlow digitizes front-desk operations for small clinics: patient intake, appointment scheduling with conflict detection, electronic medical record notes, and automated invoice generation. Built with PHP and MySQL, the system enforces role-based access (receptionist, doctor, admin) and includes input validation and audit logging for HIPAA-style compliance awareness.

projects.title: InvenTrack — Smart Inventory Manager
projects.summary: A real-time inventory and warehouse tracking dashboard with low-stock alerts and supplier management.
projects.description: InvenTrack helps small businesses track stock levels across multiple warehouses, set automatic reorder thresholds, and manage supplier relationships. Built with Vue.js and Firebase for real-time sync, the project demonstrates dynamic dashboards with live charts, CSV import/export, and role-based permissions for staff vs. managers.
projects.team_members: Faisal Al-Mutairi, Reem Al-Ghamdi, Khalid Al-Shehri

projects.title: BookNest — Online Bookstore
projects.summary: A responsive online bookstore with a recommendation engine and wishlist functionality.
projects.description: BookNest is a full e-commerce bookstore featuring catalog search and filtering, a recommendation engine based on browsing history, wishlists, and a secure checkout flow. Built with Django and PostgreSQL, it demonstrates server-side rendering, session-based auth, and payment gateway integration.

projects.title: CampusEats — Food Ordering Platform
projects.summary: A mobile-friendly food ordering platform connecting students with on-campus cafés and food trucks.
projects.description: CampusEats lets students browse menus from campus vendors, place orders for pickup, and track order status in real time. The project covers a full ordering workflow, vendor-side order management dashboard, and push notifications, built with React Native (web build) and a Node.js/Express + MongoDB backend.
projects.team_members: Hassan Al-Amri, Lina Al-Faraj, Turki Al-Rashid

projects.title: SkillSwap — Peer Tutoring Marketplace
projects.summary: A platform connecting students who want to teach and learn skills from one another, with built-in scheduling.
projects.description: SkillSwap matches students offering tutoring in one subject with students seeking help in another, using a credit-based exchange system instead of cash. Features include profile ratings, calendar-based session booking, and in-app messaging. Built with Next.js, Prisma, and SQLite.

projects.title: PMU Alumni Connect
projects.summary: A directory and networking portal linking current MIS students with PMU alumni for mentorship.
projects.description: One of the club's earliest projects: a searchable alumni directory with mentorship request workflows and event announcements. Built with plain PHP and MySQL as a foundational full-stack exercise.
projects.team_members: Fahad Abanmi and the founding MIS Club team

projects.title: EventHub PMU
projects.summary: A campus events listing and RSVP system used by student clubs to publicize activities.
projects.description: EventHub allowed clubs across PMU to post events, manage RSVPs, and send reminder emails to attendees. Built with vanilla JavaScript and a lightweight Express backend, it served as an early demonstration of dynamic content rendering without a frontend framework.

settings.mission_text: The MIS Club brings together Management Information Systems students to design, build, and ship real-world web and e-commerce projects — turning coursework into a public portfolio and giving members hands-on experience with the full development lifecycle.
